1.7 Interpret the Python reports

summary.json is updated after each completed batch. Its final complete flag means all candidate pairs in the full inventory were processed. It can be true while some left files are missing or different. Missing filenames have no candidate pairs, so an empty candidate workload is not proof of coverage of a nonempty left root.

left_files_covered counts unique left paths, separately for raw, all-images and metadata preservation. left_subsumed_by_right compares each count with the entire left inventory:

Field Acceptance
raw At least one right candidate has equal raw pages
all_images A matching candidate has equal raw and auxiliary pages
metadata_preserved A raw-equal candidate has successful metadata extraction, no warnings, and no removed or changed embedded fields

Added embedded metadata is allowed by metadata_preserved. That field does not include arbitrary uninterpreted bytes or guarantee that the auxiliary images are equal: these are independent conditions. The qualifying candidate may differ between coverage categories. Consult the individual pair records to identify a specific copy satisfying all the conditions you need.

counts reports pairs and verdicts, not unique image coverage. A duplicate-name workload can have both raw_different and raw_equal pairs while the left file is fully covered by one equal candidate. metadata_patterns groups recurring sets of changes; metadata_tags includes frequencies and at most three examples per changed field. verified_payload_bytes is aggregated from pair results, including reused results; it is not necessarily physical I/O in this invocation.

pairs.jsonl is the detailed evidence. unmatched.json lists missing left names and all duplicate-name candidate sets. At normal completion, not-confirmed.json lists left paths without a confirmed raw copy, including untested paths from a sample. It can be absent or stale after an interruption, so use the current summary and pair/cache evidence in that case.

Exit status is 0 for complete left raw coverage, 1 for unconfirmed coverage, 2 for argument errors, and 130 for a caught keyboard interruption. Metadata changes alone do not fail the raw verdict. Read failures and source changes remain errors, rather than equal results.
